title: Injective logarithmic charts preserve log regularity and recover divisorial structure
statement: Let $(Y,M_Y)$ and $(X,M_X)$ be locally Noetherian fine saturated log schemes, and let $f:(X,M_X)\to(Y,M_Y)$ be a morphism of log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Suppose $(Y,M_Y)$ is log regular in the stratum and dimension sense of that definition. Assume that etale locally on $X,Y$ the morphism has charts $P\to M_Y$, $Q\to M_X$ by fine saturated monoids $P,Q$ (as in that definition) and a homomorphism $g:P\to Q$ compatible with the structure maps and with $f$, for which $g^{\rm gp}:P^{\rm gp}\to Q^{\rm gp}$ is injective and its cokernel is torsion-free, and the comparison morphism $X\to Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] or etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Here $\mathbf Z[S]$ is the monoid ring, freely generated as an abelian group by $[s]$ with $[s][t]=[s+t]$. Then $(X,M_X)$ is log regular. Its triviality locus $U$ is dense open and, for $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the structure map canonically identifies $M_X$ with $\mathcal O_X\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$. In particular $(X,X\setminus U)$ is a log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

source.place: Expose VI 1.8 (log-smooth preservation, printed p. 70), 1.4 (dense triviality locus and recovery of the divisorial structure, printed p. 69), and the injective-chart log-smooth test used in Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71; general chart criterion: Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie (1988), Theorem 3.5 (not locally available).

proof.text: Work on affine etale chart neighbourhoods $X_0$ of $X$ and $Y_0$ of $Y$. An etale comparison is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. By [lem-trf-fs-chart-free-factorization] choose $q_1,\ldots,q_r\in Q$ such that $h:R=P\oplus\mathbf N^r\to Q$, $h(p,n)=g(p)+\sum_in_iq_i$, is injective with $h^{\rm gp}$ an isomorphism; $h$ extends $g$. The fs conditions for $R$ hold componentwise.

source.place: VI 1.9, final injective-chart test; algebraic factorization supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Write $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}C$ (log regular, having the geometric stalks of $Y$), with chart $P\to M_{Y_0}$ and structure map $\alpha:P\to C$. Give $W=\operatorname{Spec}C[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ the $R$-chart $(p,n)\mapsto\alpha(p)t^n$. It is locally Noetherian fs log regular by [lem-trf-polynomial-log-chart-regularity]. Since $\mathbf Z[R]=\mathbf Z[P][t]$, the scheme $Z=Y_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ equals $W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[R]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$: the tensor relations evaluate $t_i$ at $[q_i]$, giving inverse maps on rings.

source.place: VI 1.8--1.9, chart reduction; explicit monoid-ring calculation.

proof.text: For any geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$, [lem-trf-toric-chart-strict-local-preparation] supplies a local map $A\to B$ at a prime over $\mathfrak m_A$, where $A=\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{W,\bar w}$, the faces $G=h^{-1}(F)$, sharp monoids $S,T$, nonunit ideal $J$, and a sharp chart with its unit character and compatible completed presentation. Apply [lem-trf-formal-chart-geometric-regularity] to the same $W,R,Q,h,A,B$, faces and compatible chart data; $h^{\rm gp}$ is an isomorphism by step 1. Its stratum and dimension conclusions prove log regularity of $Z$ at every point. Empty $Z$ requires no check.

source.place: VI 1.6 models used for the independent toric calculation; formal monoid extension and dimension inputs are explicitly separated.

proof.text:
The smooth comparison $X_0\to Z$ has the associated $Q$-chart on both sides, so its source log structure is the pullback. At compatible geometric points use the canonical strict-henselization map and let $A=\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X_0,\bar x}$, and $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ be the nonunit ideal of $A$. Local maps reflect units, so the characteristic stays of rank $\rho$ and the source ideal is $IB$ by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. By [lem-trf-smooth-geometric-stalk-algebra], $A\to B$ and $A/I\to B/IB$ are Noetherian flat local maps with the same regular closed fibre $F$. Since $A/I$ is regular, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] makes $B/IB$ regular. Specializing [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] at the maximal ideals for both flat local maps,
$$\dim B=\dim A+\dim F=\dim(A/I)+\rho+\dim F=\dim(B/IB)+\rho.$$
Hence $X_0$ is log regular. The etale charts cover every geometric point of $X$, giving log regularity of $X$ by its geometric-stalk definition.

source.place: Tags 031E and 00ON, applied to the strict smooth comparison in ILO VI 1.8.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], the triviality locus $U$ of $X$ is open dense and $M_X=\mathcal O_X\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$ via the structure map. With $D=X\setminus U$, this is exactly the divisorial log structure of [def-trf-log-regular-pair]; it is fs log regular and its triviality locus is $U$. Thus $(X,D)$ is a log regular pair, also when $X$ or $D$ is empty.

source.place: VI 1.4, printed p. 69; VIII 3.4.1, printed p. 110.

lean.statement: theorem logSmooth_logRegular (X Y : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (f : EtaleLogHom X Y) (hY : Y.IsLogRegular) (hcharts : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme), ∃ c : InjectiveFSLogChart X Y f, Nonempty ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale t).fiber.obj c.V) ∧ (Smooth c.comparison ∨ Etale c.comparison)) : X.IsLogRegular ∧ ∃ (U : X.scheme.Opens) (hd : DenseRange U.ι), X.logStructure.trivialityLocus = (U : Set X.scheme) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf X.scheme.smallEtaleTopology (divisorialLogPresheaf U.ι) ∧ (∃ e : X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf U.ι, e.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap U.ι = X.logStructure.alpha) ∧ @IsDivisorialFineSaturatedLogRegularPair X.scheme U.toScheme U.ι inferInstance X.locallyNoetherian hd
